findings.evidence: tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:1082,1091,1100,1109,1118,1127 each require401 AND no operational records from each supplying family, explicitly reusing the same measured shared-bootstrap request/result. This duplicates the whole-response confidentiality/status predicate across the six screen rows instead of limiting each confidentiality row to its owned data.
findings.counterexample: A permitted common-bootstrap implementation returns401 to anonymous callers and withholds requisitions, equity, referrals and audit/receipts, but accidentally includes only offer records in the error body. The Offers protection is defective; the other data families remain withheld. Every one of the six rows nevertheless fails its global no-operational-records predicate when reusing that same response. An otherwise identical app with separate read endpoints loses only the affected family credit. This is a source counterexample, not an executed mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Give HTTP401 enforcement a single explicit owner for each distinct observed request family/shared response, and scope each confidentiality outcome to its owned data; reuse shared-response data slices without applying an unrelated leaked collection to every screen. Preserve the public no-anonymous-data/status requirements and the original total weight pool.

findings.evidence: judge.toml:1028 requires creation with actual session actor and saved/audit attribution. Public hireops_rules.md:389-400 mandates append-only actor-bearing audit/receipts for approve/revise/rescind; requisition creation only requires signed-in permission, saved identity/details and ignored optional claims (lines38-39,205-215,374-383). No public requirement mandates storing/exposing a requisition creator. Golden does expose it through src/index.js:304, but that cannot create a public demand.
findings.counterexample: A conforming app authenticates every requisition creation, ignores all seven claims and saves the correct ID/title/department/budget, but intentionally has no requisition creator field or creation audit row. The new criterion can withhold credit because no saved actor attribution exists, despite identical valid behavior with and without claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Require equivalent authorized creation and unchanged legitimate values; compare actual-session attribution only wherever the product already records/exposes it, without requiring a new creator field or creation-audit feature.

findings.evidence: judge.toml:1280 demands headroom -10 after approval, :1289 -10 after revision, and :1298 +20 after rescission. These fixed settlement amounts remain part of the dashboard rows even though movement/formula correctness has other owners and prompt.md:54 says to use recorded ledger facts.
findings.counterexample: An independent settlement bug records -11 instead of -10 for the valid base10 approval. The requisition headroom and dashboard correctly sum the actual persisted -11 movement and status counts. The settlement owner should fail, but hro_dashboard_approval also fails the demanded -10, removing valid aggregation credit. Corresponding revision/release amount bugs produce the same duplicate deduction.
findings.suggested_fix: After each independently successful transition, compare dashboard aggregates/counts with observed persisted requisition headroom, movements and statuses; retain raw-input numerical settlement expectations in their existing formula/ledger owners.

limits: This report closes only the stated source defects on the recorded live hashes and identifies three remaining focused refinements. It does not refute or clear the completed audit, shared-template blockers, runtime evidence gaps, workload, Oracle/model scores, or packaging readiness.
